description: xlwings is a Python library that makes it easy to call Python from Excel and vice versa. It works with Excel on Windows, macOS, and Excel on the web.

summary.one_liner: xlwings is a Python library for calling Python from Excel and Excel from Python, for scripting, macros, and user-defined functions.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes xlwings as a BSD-licensed Python library with three main uses: scripting (automating and interacting with Excel from Python using syntax close to VBA), macros (replacing VBA macros with Python code), and UDFs (writing user-defined functions in Python, Windows only). It states that NumPy arrays and Pandas Series/DataFrames are fully supported. Workbooks built with xlwings are described as easy to distribute and working on Windows and macOS. The README also covers xlwings Lite, which runs Python inside Excel without a local Python install and stores the code in the workbook, and xlwings PRO, a separately licensed add-on with a server component, a template-based reporting system, and a faster reader alternative to pandas.read_excel(). The PRO parts are source available under dual licenses, with noncommercial use free.
use_cases: automate Excel workbooks from Python scripts
replace VBA macros with Python code
write custom Excel functions in Python
pass pandas DataFrames and NumPy arrays to Excel
distribute Excel workbooks that run Python logic
run Python inside Excel without a local install
how_to_run: Install xlwings from Python (the README does not give explicit install commands in this excerpt)
notable: Scripting syntax designed to be close to VBA
User-defined functions in Python (Windows only, per README)
